No, that statement is not accurate. The Swiss Criminal Code (Strafgesetzbuch, StGB) does include provisions that protect against hate speech and discrimination based on sexual orientation.

Specifically, Article 261bis of the Swiss Criminal Code prohibits public incitement to hatred or discrimination against a person or a group of persons on account of their race, ethnicity, religion, or sexual orientation. The law has been interpreted and applied to cover discrimination based on sexual orientation, including homosexuality.

While the original formulation of the law focused on race, ethnicity, and religion, subsequent legal interpretations and amendments have expanded its scope to include sexual orientation as a protected characteristic. Therefore, hate speech targeting individuals based on their homosexuality is indeed criminalized under Swiss law.
